analysis: Three changes were reviewed. (1) docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md is shown only as head text with no patch, so changed lines can't be isolated. The visible content is consistent with the T-041 posture: HMAC lookup tags, DBK3 AES-GCM with a KEK in the Secure Enclave and Keychain, a 1800s TTL ceiling (line 277), per-file epoch handling, a rolling-day write ledger, CacheVolume checks, and O_NONBLOCK no-follow opens (lines 68-75). No doc claim loosens a documented control or contradicts the threat model. The 90% novel-checkpoint sub-budget and demand gate (line 279) are write-wear and availability controls, not disclosure changes. (2) libs/mlx-swift-lm is bumped from 14661d9 to 2068c93. Only the pointers are visible, with no diff. The doc text suggests this submodule carries changes to checkpoint import staging (host-zero destinations, line 119), bounded fallback retry (lines 174-197) and read budgets. Those touch the TB-007 and T-041 surface (decrypted KV and checkpoint handling, memory reservation, cache identity binding). They cannot be assessed from this input, which is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety. (3) The new ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift is a test-only, opt-in file (DARKBLOOM_RESTORE_CONTENTION_BENCHMARK=1). It writes a timing report to a new absolute path and uses tenant-scoped foreign requests so it does not share checkpoints across scopes. It is not production code and adds no production attack surface. The next pass should inspect the mlx-swift-lm diff for T-041, T-028 and TB-007: staging allocation bounds, retry and fallback authority, identity binding, and plaintext residue in host buffers.
